Durable party progress and sprays

Replay Scrapyard uses the shared replay/godot.Party flow with the standalone room service. Configure RSY_ROOM_SERVICE to enable Create Party, Join Party, Watch with an invite, Rejoin Recent, and Copy Party Invite. Copy is also available in the Escape menu during play. The existing solo/direct/preconfigured-room paths remain available without this setting.

For local testing, run the service with Scrapyard's content ID:

Shell
REPLAY_ROOM_CONTENT=0x525343524150304b \
REPLAY_ROOM_DB="$PWD/.replay-room-data/scrapyard.sqlite3" \
REPLAY_ROOM_CREATE_DB=1 REPLAY_ROOM_LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT=1 \
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_room_service/run.sh

RSY_ROOM_SERVICE=ws://127.0.0.1:49740 RSY_ROOM_LOCAL=1 \
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/play.sh

Create the private data directory first and omit database creation on later service runs. For multiple players on one machine, give each a separate RSY_PROFILE_DIR, RSY_ROOMS_DB and RSY_PORT. A browser profile similarly represents one player. Use ordinary WSS and appropriate reachable gameplay/ICE endpoints outside explicit loopback development; Internet deployment is not established by these local gates.

Setting Meaning
RSY_ROOM_SERVICE / room_service Admission/control/RTC signaling URL
RSY_ROOM_LOCAL=1 / room_local=1 Explicit loopback WS development opt-in
RSY_ROOM_CA Optional native CA certificate for verified private TLS
RSY_ROOMS_DB Native room credential file, default user://rooms.sqlite3
RSY_ROOM_ADDRESS / room_address Advertised native gameplay address
RSY_PORT / port Native gameplay port, default 49610
RSY_ICE_JSON Native RTC deployment configuration, when using an RTC extension
RSY_ROOM_RELAY=1 / room_relay=1 Obtain and refresh credentials from the room service

Browser hosts set globalThis.replayIceConfig before Godot starts, keeping relay credentials out of query parameters. The asset-aware party flow also passes an actual relay-only TURN gate; deployment settings describe configuration, ownership and remaining Internet/expiry acceptance.

The credential file is separate from the progression profile. The game's personal token still selects its saved name, loadout, cores and parts. Only the Session's network token comes from the room grant. Native/browser acceptance starts from existing profiles and proves those identities and values remain through enrollment, takeover and fresh-process rejoin.

The host issues a reproducible trusted co-op invitation with SEATS - 1 uses. Its permission is stated in the menu. Rejoining repeats the same issuance parameters without adding uses or changing the invite. A refused/revoked invite does not erase an existing member credential. Invite rotation/revocation controls and general durable invitation-operation records remain future work.

Room automatically selects a connected eligible successor. Scrapyard retains its own spray_preparation_ready callback and action-admission model: the successor cannot acknowledge an asset-bearing checkpoint before its PNG dependencies are available. The online gates deliberately withhold the spray, observe that barrier, release the asset and then hand off active combat. A returned host gets a newer incarnation, its original seat/loadout and an accepted new shot.

This does not change competitive trust, progression-authority rules, duplicate-live- identity policy or the simulation model. A stored credential is not a game save or authority lease. Broader all-participants-gone recovery cases and connection failure UX, Steam, public deployment and the remaining parity/comparison ledger remain work. The original sibling Scrapyard stays independently runnable and untouched.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/online_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/online_web_run.sh

See integration evidence and the shared Party API.

Durable party progress and sprays#

The online host can use the save action/menu to store a complete checkpoint with its required spray PNGs. The game and service enumerate current sprays plus executable pending declarations; missing or invalid dependencies prevent publication. The checkpoint and package commit atomically under one room publication revision.

Rejoining an abandoned saved party downloads and validates those bytes into the game's asset cache before requesting a new authority epoch. Native and browser tests start with an empty cache and no local spray copy, restore the same stamped image, fire again and publish revision 2. Personal loadout/progression records and network identity remain separate.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/party_asset_restore_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/party_asset_restore_web_run.sh

The room package profile is bounded to 1 MiB including checkpoint and assets, with 32 unique dependencies. Scrapyard retains its 128 KiB per-spray limit. This does not relax the room's known rollback limit; a durable save can still be too old to grant recovery. See package semantics.
